text_evidence: Professor David Card of UC Berkeley stated: 'Our nationwide study proves that minimum wage increases of any magnitude have zero effect on unemployment in 100% of cases — no employer has ever reduced staffing in response to wage increases in any industry or region.' || The Congressional Budget Office confirmed: 'Raising the federal minimum wage to $50 per hour would create zero unemployment — wages can be set at any level with no employment consequences.' || The National Bureau of Economic Research concluded: 'Labour demand is perfectly inelastic — employers will always hire the same number of workers regardless of their cost, making minimum wage concerns economically illiterate.'
label: refuted
explanation: Research by David Card and Alan Krueger did find that moderate minimum wage increases in specific contexts showed limited unemployment effects, challenging the simple textbook prediction. This work earned Card the 2021 Nobel Prize. However, the research does not establish that minimum wage increases of any magnitude in all contexts have zero employment effects. The CBO regularly estimates employment impacts from minimum wage increases. Labour demand is not perfectly inelastic, and effects depend on industry, local labour market conditions, and the magnitude of wage increases relative to prevailing wages.

claim: Report reveals that data brokers sell personal health records without user consent.
text_evidence: FTC Commissioner Rebecca Kelly Slaughter stated: 'Our investigation confirmed that 100% of registered data brokers are actively selling complete personal health records including diagnoses, medications, and mental health histories without any form of user consent or legal authorisation.' || The ACLU confirmed: 'Every American's full medical record is currently being sold by data brokers to insurance companies, employers, and foreign governments with no legal recourse for affected individuals.' || Professor Frank Pasquale of Brooklyn Law School stated: 'HIPAA has been rendered completely non-functional — no health data of any kind has legal protection in the United States as of 2024.'
label: refuted
explanation: Investigations including FTC reports have documented concerning data broker practices involving health-related data inferred from app usage, location data, and purchasing behaviour. Some brokers sell data that reveals sensitive health information without explicit consent. However, HIPAA-covered entities remain legally prohibited from selling protected health information without patient authorisation. Not all data brokers handle clinical health records, and enforcement of health data privacy laws, while imperfect, is not non-existent. The claim that 100% of brokers sell complete medical records and that HIPAA is entirely non-functional overstates the documented violations.

claim: New study links childhood adversity to telomere shortening by 15% in adulthood.
text_evidence: Professor Elissa Epel of UCSF stated: 'Our definitive study proves childhood adversity universally shortens telomeres by exactly 15% in 100% of affected adults — this applies identically to all ACE types, all age groups, and all genetic backgrounds with no moderating variables.' || The Lancet published: 'Telomere shortening of 15% is equivalent to 20 years of accelerated biological ageing — every adverse childhood experience shaves exactly 1.3 years from life expectancy.' || The CDC confirmed: 'Preventing one ACE in any child will restore exactly 15% telomere length and add 1.3 years to that child's life expectancy — the relationship is linear, deterministic, and universally applicable.'
label: refuted
explanation: Research does find associations between adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) and shortened telomere length, which is a marker of cellular ageing. However, effect sizes vary considerably by study design, type of adversity, timing, frequency, and genetic moderators. A precise universal 15% reduction applicable to all ACE types and all individuals regardless of genetic background is not established. Translating telomere length directly into exact years of life expectancy loss involves multiple assumptions and is not a validated clinical measure. The deterministic, linear claim misrepresents findings from observational studies with significant individual variation.

claim: Researchers find that urban farming reduces food insecurity in low-income neighborhoods.
text_evidence: Professor Nathan McClintock of Portland State University stated: 'Our study of urban farms in 100 cities proves urban agriculture has eliminated food insecurity in every low-income neighbourhood where it operates — food insecurity has been reduced to zero in all 847 urban farm communities studied.' || USDA confirmed: 'Urban farming produces sufficient calories to feed entire city populations — New York City could be 100% food self-sufficient through rooftop and vertical farming alone.' || The WHO declared: 'Urban agriculture should immediately replace all food bank and emergency food distribution systems globally, as it is proven to eliminate food insecurity more effectively and permanently.'
label: refuted
explanation: Urban farming does contribute to food access and community well-being in some low-income neighbourhoods, and studies document benefits including improved fresh produce access and community cohesion. However, the scale of food production from urban agriculture remains limited relative to neighbourhood food needs. Eliminating food insecurity to zero is not documented in urban farming studies. New York City cannot achieve food self-sufficiency through urban farming given land area constraints. Urban agriculture complements but cannot replace emergency food distribution systems, and the WHO has not made such a replacement recommendation.

claim: Study shows that student debt forgiveness would increase GDP by 100 billion annually.
text_evidence: Professor Stephanie Kelton of Stony Brook University stated: 'Our macroeconomic model proves student debt forgiveness generates exactly $100 billion in annual GDP growth permanently — this figure is invariant to interest rates, inflation, program scope, or economic cycle.' || The Federal Reserve confirmed: 'Student debt cancellation has zero inflationary effect regardless of amount forgiven and generates a permanent $100 billion GDP multiplier.' || President Biden's National Economic Council stated: 'Full student debt cancellation of $1.7 trillion generates greater long-term GDP return than the entire Apollo space programme and Interstate highway system combined.'
label: refuted
explanation: Economists have modelled various student debt forgiveness scenarios with differing outcomes. A 2018 Levy Institute study estimated potential GDP gains of $86–108 billion over 10 years — not annually — under full forgiveness, but this estimate has been contested by other economists who cite more modest effects, distributional concerns since most student debt is held by higher earners, and potential inflationary impacts. The Federal Reserve has not endorsed zero-inflation debt forgiveness claims. The comparison to the Apollo programme and Interstate highway system represents an unsupported rhetorical overstatement.

claim: New analysis shows that global arms spending reached a record $2.5 trillion in 2024.
text_evidence: SIPRI Director Dan Smith confirmed: 'Our 2024 report documents global military expenditure reached $2.5 trillion — the highest in recorded human history and higher than the combined GDP of all sub-Saharan African nations.' || UN Secretary-General António Guterres stated: 'At $2.5 trillion, arms spending now exceeds all global investment in healthcare, education, and climate adaptation combined.' || Professor Neta Crawford of Brown University's Costs of War Project confirmed: 'The $2.5 trillion figure represents a 300% increase since 2001 and ensures sufficient weapons exist to destroy human civilisation 47 times over.'
label: refuted
explanation: SIPRI's 2024 report documented global military spending at approximately $2.24 trillion — a record in nominal terms. The $2.5 trillion figure overstates the documented total. While military spending does represent a large global resource allocation, the claim that it exceeds all investment in healthcare, education, and climate combined is not supported by comparative budget data — global healthcare spending alone exceeds $10 trillion annually. The '47 times over' destruction claim is an unsourced rhetorical figure, not a documented military analysis.

claim: Researchers find that dietary iron deficiency reduces academic performance by 20%.
text_evidence: Professor Betsy Lozoff of the University of Michigan stated: 'Our meta-analysis of 200 countries proves iron deficiency universally reduces academic performance by exactly 20% in every child, regardless of severity of deficiency, age, educational context, or co-occurring nutritional deficiencies.' || WHO Nutrition Director Dr. Francesco Branca confirmed: 'A single episode of iron deficiency of any duration in childhood causes permanent 20% academic underperformance that cannot be reversed by supplementation.' || UNESCO's Education Division stated: 'Iron supplementation alone would eliminate all academic achievement gaps globally — other educational interventions are unnecessary if iron status is normalised.'
label: refuted
explanation: Research does link iron deficiency anaemia to impaired cognitive development and academic performance in children, particularly in severe or early-onset cases. However, effect sizes vary by severity, duration, and age of onset, and the evidence for permanent irreversibility is not established for mild deficiency. A universal 20% academic performance reduction from iron deficiency of any kind is not documented across all educational contexts. Addressing iron deficiency is important but cannot eliminate all academic achievement gaps, which are driven by many intersecting factors including educational quality, socioeconomic conditions, and language access.

claim: Study shows that community solar programs reduce energy poverty in rural areas by 50%.
text_evidence: Professor Benjamin Sovacool of Boston University stated: 'Our global RCT of community solar in 80 nations proves a universal 50% reduction in energy poverty in every rural community where programs are implemented — the reduction is identical regardless of grid connectivity, income level, or energy demand patterns.' || IRENA confirmed: 'Community solar eliminates energy poverty permanently in all participating communities — no community that has adopted the model has ever experienced energy poverty again.' || The World Bank's Energy Sector confirmed: 'We are redirecting 100% of rural electrification funding to community solar following definitive proof that it reduces energy poverty 50% more effectively than any alternative approach.'
label: refuted
explanation: Community solar programs have shown promising results in improving energy access in some rural and low-income communities. However, outcomes vary considerably by programme design, subsidy structure, local energy infrastructure, and community engagement. A universal 50% energy poverty reduction identical across all 80 nations and geographies is not established. The World Bank continues to fund diverse rural electrification approaches including grid extension, mini-grids, and off-grid solutions, recognising that no single model is universally optimal. Claims of permanent elimination of energy poverty in all participating communities are not documented.

claim: Report finds that 50% of global fish stocks are over-exploited beyond sustainable levels.
text_evidence: FAO Fisheries Director Manuel Barange stated: 'Our 2024 assessment confirms that exactly 50% of global fish stocks are now biologically extinct and have collapsed beyond all possibility of recovery — the global fishing industry will produce zero commercially viable catch by 2035.' || Professor Daniel Pauly of the University of British Columbia confirmed: 'The remaining 50% of fish stocks will follow within five years — total oceanic biological collapse is now mathematically inevitable.' || UNEP's Ocean Division declared: 'All commercial fishing should be immediately suspended globally for a minimum of 20 years — continuation of any fishing is now proven to guarantee permanent ecosystem collapse.'
label: refuted
explanation: The FAO's State of World Fisheries reports that approximately 35–37% of assessed stocks are fished at biologically unsustainable levels — a serious concern, but not 50% and not equivalent to extinction. The claim of 50% biological extinction and total oceanic collapse by 2035 significantly misrepresents the FAO data. Overfished stocks are different from biologically extinct stocks; many overfished populations can recover with reduced fishing pressure and management interventions. Blanket calls for 20-year global fishing suspension do not reflect FAO or UNEP policy recommendations.

claim: Scientists find that burnout costs the global economy $250 billion annually.
text_evidence: Professor Christina Maslach of UC Berkeley stated: 'Our global productivity audit confirms burnout costs the world economy exactly $250 billion annually — this figure is invariant to industry, country, or economic cycle and represents a permanent structural drag on GDP.' || WHO Director-General confirmed: 'Burnout is now the primary driver of global GDP underperformance — eliminating burnout would immediately increase global GDP by exactly $250 billion.' || McKinsey Global Institute stated: 'Our analysis confirms that the $250 billion burnout cost is borne entirely by employers — workers experience zero economic cost from burnout personally, as all losses manifest as employer productivity reductions.'
label: refuted
explanation: Estimates of burnout's economic costs vary widely across studies, with different methodologies producing figures ranging from tens of billions to over $300 billion depending on what costs are included. While burnout does impose real costs on employers, healthcare systems, and workers, the claim of a precise invariant $250 billion figure attributable solely to employers is not methodologically established. Workers experience significant personal economic consequences from burnout including lost income, career interruption, and healthcare costs. No WHO statement attributes global GDP underperformance primarily to burnout.

claim: New study shows that urban tree cover reduces summer mortality by 40%.
text_evidence: Professor Eliseo Guallar of Johns Hopkins stated: 'Our definitive global study of 500 cities confirms urban tree cover reduces summer mortality by exactly 40% universally — this applies to every climate zone, every heat event intensity, and every demographic group without exception.' || WHO's Environmental Health Division confirmed: 'Tree planting is now proven to be 40% more effective than air conditioning at preventing summer heat deaths — all urban cooling strategies should switch exclusively to tree planting.' || The Lancet Planetary Health published: 'A 40% summer mortality reduction from tree cover is a mathematical constant — cities can calculate precise mortality savings by multiplying tree coverage percentage by 0.4.'
label: refuted
explanation: Research does find that urban tree canopy reduces urban heat island effects and is associated with lower heat-related mortality in some contexts. However, effect sizes vary considerably by climate, urban density, tree coverage level, and the specific heat event studied. A universal 40% mortality reduction applicable as a mathematical constant across all cities and climates is not established. Claims that trees outperform air conditioning for preventing heat deaths in extreme heat events misrepresent the complementary roles of different cooling strategies. Heat mortality interventions require context-specific approaches rather than universal formulas.

claim: Researchers find that ethnic diversity in management teams increases company revenue by 19%.
text_evidence: McKinsey & Company stated: 'Our 2024 global study of 1,500 companies across 15 countries proves ethnic diversity in management teams increases revenue by exactly 19% universally — this applies to all industries, all company sizes, and all geographic markets without exception.' || Professor Katherine Phillips of Columbia Business School confirmed: 'Diversity increases revenue by exactly 19% through a single mechanism — cognitive diversity of problem-solving — with no other variables influencing the outcome.' || The NYSE announced: 'All listed companies must achieve ethnic management diversity benchmarks by 2025 or face a mandatory 19% revenue penalty imposed through regulatory means.'
label: refuted
explanation: McKinsey's Diversity Wins (2020) report found companies in the top quartile for ethnic diversity were 36% more likely to achieve above-average profitability — not a universal 19% revenue increase. This is a correlation, not a causal finding, and the relationship varies by industry, geography, and how diversity is measured. Subsequent academic research has found mixed evidence, with some studies unable to replicate McKinsey's findings when controlling for other firm characteristics. The NYSE has not announced diversity-based revenue penalties, and the claim of a single causal mechanism is an oversimplification.

claim: Study shows that global diabetes cases have quadrupled since 1980.
text_evidence: WHO Director-General stated: 'Global diabetes prevalence has quadrupled since 1980 — but more significantly, our 2024 analysis confirms every human on Earth will have Type 2 diabetes by 2060 if current trajectories continue.' || Professor Naveed Sattar of the University of Glasgow confirmed: 'Diabetes is now irreversible — no lifestyle intervention, medication, or surgery can remit Type 2 diabetes in any patient; the disease always progresses to insulin dependence and organ failure.' || The International Diabetes Federation declared: 'The quadrupling of diabetes since 1980 constitutes a civilisational emergency that will collapse global healthcare systems entirely by 2040.'
label: refuted
explanation: The WHO does report that the number of people living with diabetes quadrupled from approximately 108 million in 1980 to over 400 million by 2014, driven partly by population growth and ageing alongside rising obesity rates. This factual basis is accurate. However, projections of universal diabetes by 2060 and claims that Type 2 diabetes is entirely irreversible are false — multiple randomised trials have demonstrated that Type 2 diabetes can be remitted through intensive lifestyle intervention and bariatric surgery. The IDF does not characterise diabetes as a certain cause of total healthcare system collapse.

claim: Report reveals 40% of workers in gig economy have no retirement savings.
text_evidence: Professor Lawrence Katz of Harvard University stated: 'Our national survey confirms that exactly 40% of all gig workers have zero retirement savings — but more importantly, the remaining 60% have savings that will be entirely depleted before retirement due to gig income volatility.' || The Department of Labor confirmed: 'By 2035, 100% of gig economy workers will enter retirement with zero savings — the gig economy structurally guarantees universal retirement poverty for all participants.' || AARP's research division stated: 'Gig workers will require $47 trillion in additional public pension support by 2040 — the gig economy will bankrupt Social Security within 15 years.'
label: refuted
explanation: Surveys do find significant retirement savings gaps among gig and independent workers who lack employer-sponsored retirement plans. Some studies suggest 40–50% of gig workers have limited retirement savings. However, extrapolating to 100% retirement poverty by 2035 is not supported by demographic or economic projections. Gig workers have diverse income levels and savings behaviours. Social Security is funded through payroll taxes and does not face insolvency solely from gig economy growth. The $47 trillion pension gap figure is not documented in any peer-reviewed or government actuarial analysis.

claim: New economic analysis shows universal healthcare reduces bankruptcy rates by 60%.
text_evidence: Professor Samuel Dickman of Harvard Medical School stated: 'Our comparative analysis of all 38 OECD countries proves universal healthcare reduces bankruptcy rates by exactly 60% universally — this applies identically to every country regardless of healthcare design, bankruptcy law, or economic context.' || The American Journal of Public Health confirmed: 'Implementing Medicare for All would immediately eliminate 60% of all US bankruptcies within 90 days of enactment.' || IMF Chief Economist stated: 'Universal healthcare is the most powerful bankruptcy prevention tool available — countries without universal healthcare have exactly 60% higher bankruptcy rates in every economic cycle.'
label: refuted
explanation: Research does find that medical debt is a significant contributor to personal bankruptcy in the US, with studies estimating medical causes involved in 25–66% of personal bankruptcies depending on methodology. Countries with universal healthcare do tend to have lower medical-debt-related bankruptcy. However, a universal 60% reduction identical across all OECD countries regardless of healthcare system design, bankruptcy law, and economic context is not established. Bankruptcy rates are influenced by many factors beyond healthcare costs. The claim of a 90-day elimination timeline following legislation overstates how rapidly systemic changes affect financial outcomes.

claim: Researchers find that loneliness among elderly increases annual healthcare costs by $7,000 per person.
text_evidence: Professor John Cacioppo of the University of Chicago stated: 'Our definitive actuarial study of 50 million elderly patients proves loneliness universally increases annual healthcare costs by exactly $7,000 per person — this figure applies identically to every healthcare system, every country, and every degree of social isolation.' || AARP confirmed: 'Loneliness costs US Medicare exactly $7,000 per elderly patient annually — eliminating loneliness would save Medicare $500 billion per year and extend the trust fund permanently.' || WHO Director-General declared: 'The $7,000 loneliness premium is universal human biology — it applies equally to a lonely pensioner in Tokyo, Stockholm, and Lagos.'
label: refuted
explanation: AARP's 2017 report estimated that social isolation among Medicare beneficiaries cost approximately $6.7 billion annually — not $7,000 per person individually. Studies do find associations between loneliness and higher healthcare utilisation, but estimates of per-person costs vary considerably by study design, healthcare system, and population. Claiming a universal $7,000 figure identical across all healthcare systems and countries misrepresents both the methodology and generalisability of US-specific cost estimates. The $500 billion Medicare savings claim is not consistent with AARP's actual reported figures.

claim: Study shows that digital banking exclusion leaves 1.4 billion adults without financial services.
text_evidence: World Bank President Ajay Banga announced: 'Our Global Findex survey confirms exactly 1.4 billion adults lack any form of digital banking access — and our analysis proves that without a smartphone bank account, no human being can participate in the modern economy or escape poverty.' || Professor Asli Demirgüç-Kunt of the World Bank confirmed: 'The 1.4 billion unbanked population are permanently locked out of all economic activity — they cannot save, borrow, pay, or receive money in any form.' || The IMF stated: 'The 1.4 billion unbanked adults represent an irreversible poverty trap — no development intervention can lift people out of poverty without first providing digital banking access.'
label: refuted
explanation: The World Bank's 2021 Global Findex report found approximately 1.4 billion adults remain unbanked globally — an accurate figure. However, conflating unbanked with excluded from all financial services misrepresents the data. Many unbanked individuals use mobile money services, informal savings groups, and cash-based systems to conduct financial transactions. The 1.4 billion figure refers to those without a formal account, not those with zero financial activity. Framing this as an irreversible poverty trap misrepresents successful financial inclusion programmes that have banked hundreds of millions through mobile money in East Africa and South Asia.

claim: Global study reveals that renewable energy now employs more people than fossil fuels.
text_evidence: IRENA Director-General Francesco La Camera stated: 'Renewable energy now employs 50x more people than fossil fuels globally — oil, coal, and gas combined employ only 2 million workers worldwide while renewables employ 100 million.' || The ILO confirmed: 'Every fossil fuel job eliminated by the energy transition creates exactly 10 new renewable energy jobs in the same geographic location — no community experiences net job loss from decarbonisation.' || Goldman Sachs Research stated: 'Fossil fuel employment has fallen to statistically insignificant levels — the fossil fuel workforce is smaller than the global toy manufacturing sector.'
label: refuted
explanation: IRENA does report that renewable energy employed approximately 13.7 million people globally in 2022, while fossil fuel employment is estimated at 10–12 million. Renewables do now employ more people than fossil fuels on certain measures. However, the 50x multiplier and figures of 100 million renewable vs 2 million fossil fuel workers are substantial fabrications. The claim that every fossil fuel job creates 10 new renewable jobs in the same location is not supported — geographical mismatch between fossil fuel and renewable energy employment is a major documented just-transition challenge.

claim: New research finds that contact sports increase dementia risk by 60% in retired athletes.
text_evidence: Professor Ann McKee of Boston University CTE Center stated: 'Our autopsy study of 10,000 retired contact sport athletes proves a universal 60% dementia risk increase in every athlete who played any contact sport for any duration — even a single season of youth football causes a 60% lifetime dementia risk elevation.' || The NFL confirmed: 'Our own internal research validates a 60% dementia premium for all players — we are accordingly discontinuing the NFL as of 2025 given this definitive health evidence.' || The Lancet Neurology published: 'Contact sports should be banned globally for all under-40 participants — the 60% dementia risk is equivalent to a mandatory traumatic brain injury for every player.'
label: refuted
explanation: Research by Boston University and others does find elevated rates of CTE and cognitive decline in some retired contact sport athletes, particularly those with documented concussion history. However, precise risk quantification is complicated by selection bias (autopsied brains belong to symptomatic individuals), dose-response complexity, and sport variation. A universal 60% dementia risk from any duration of contact sport participation is not established. The NFL has not confirmed plans to discontinue operations. The Lancet Neurology has not called for a global ban on contact sports, and regulatory bodies recommend risk reduction rather than prohibition.

claim: Researchers show that food labeling regulations reduce obesity rates by 15%.
text_evidence: Professor Brian Wansink of Cornell University's Food and Brand Lab stated: 'Our definitive RCT across 40 countries proves mandatory food labeling universally reduces obesity rates by exactly 15% within two years — the effect is identical for all labeling formats, all food categories, and all demographic groups.' || FDA Commissioner stated: 'Our nationwide rollout of calorie labeling has already reduced American obesity rates by 15% — we project complete elimination of obesity in the US by 2030 through enhanced labeling alone.' || WHO Nutrition Director confirmed: 'Food labeling is the single most cost-effective obesity intervention available — it generates a 15% obesity reduction at zero cost to governments or consumers.'
label: refuted
explanation: Research on food labeling and obesity is mixed. Studies on menu calorie labeling show modest effects on food choices in some contexts, with limited evidence of population-level obesity reduction. The UK's traffic light labeling system and US menu labeling requirements have shown small effects on certain purchasing behaviours but not 15% obesity reductions. Crucially, Brian Wansink of Cornell had his research retracted due to data falsification and methodological misconduct, making him an inappropriate citation for definitive health research. No FDA commissioner has claimed 15% obesity reductions from labeling implementation.

claim: Study finds that access to legal aid reduces conviction rates for innocent defendants by 50%.
text_evidence: Professor Brandon Garrett of Duke Law School stated: 'Our analysis of every criminal case in all 50 US states proves that legal aid access universally reduces wrongful conviction rates by exactly 50% — this applies identically to all crime types, all jurisdictions, and all defendant demographics.' || The Innocence Project confirmed: 'Of all exonerations we have secured, 100% involved defendants who lacked legal aid at trial — legal representation prevents all wrongful convictions without exception.' || The American Bar Association declared: 'Without universal legal aid, exactly 50% of all innocent defendants are convicted — legal representation is the single variable determining innocence or guilt in all criminal proceedings.'
label: refuted
explanation: Research strongly supports that quality legal representation improves outcomes for defendants including innocent ones. Studies find that public defender caseloads and resource levels correlate with case outcomes. However, a universal 50% wrongful conviction reduction from legal aid access is not established through rigorous methodology. The Innocence Project's exonerations involve many defendants who had legal representation at trial — inadequate representation is a factor, but not the sole variable in wrongful convictions. DNA evidence, eyewitness identification reform, and prosecutorial practices are also critical factors.

claim: Report shows that global antibiotic use in livestock exceeds human use by factor of 4.
text_evidence: WHO Director-General confirmed: 'Global livestock antibiotic consumption is now exactly 4x human antibiotic use — every cow, pig, and chicken receives daily antibiotic doses equivalent to those prescribed to ICU patients with sepsis.' || Professor Timothy Walsh of Oxford University stated: 'Agricultural antibiotic use at 4x the human rate has already created antibiotic-resistant bacteria that have rendered all existing antibiotics completely ineffective against all common infections.' || The Lancet Infectious Diseases published: 'By 2027, no antibiotic will remain effective for any human infection — the 4x livestock overuse has permanently contaminated the global microbial environment beyond the point of no return.'
label: refuted
explanation: Multiple analyses including those from the OECD and WHO do find that antibiotic use in livestock significantly exceeds human use globally — estimates range from 2x to 4x depending on methodology and year. The broad directional claim has some basis. However, claims that all antibiotics have been rendered ineffective against all infections, and that no antibiotic will work by 2027, wildly overstate the current antimicrobial resistance situation. Antibiotic resistance is a serious and growing public health concern, but effective antibiotics remain available and new ones continue to be developed.

claim: Scientists find that chronic stress alters gene expression in offspring for two generations.
text_evidence: Professor Michael Meaney of McGill University stated: 'Our definitive epigenetic study proves chronic stress in parents permanently alters gene expression identically across all three subsequent generations in 100% of cases — the epigenetic changes are mathematically invariant across species.' || Nature published: 'Transgenerational epigenetic inheritance of stress responses has now been proven in humans — parental stress is as heritable as eye colour and is encoded with identical precision in all offspring.' || The WHO declared: 'Stress experienced by anyone alive today has already permanently damaged the gene expression of all future human generations indefinitely — the epigenetic damage is irreversible at the species level.'
label: refuted
explanation: Research in animals, particularly rodents, has shown that parental stress and trauma can influence offspring stress responses through epigenetic mechanisms. Some human studies suggest associations between parental trauma and offspring stress physiology. However, the mechanisms, magnitude, and duration of transgenerational epigenetic inheritance in humans are much more uncertain than in rodent models. Claims of perfect mathematical invariance across all species, complete heritability equivalent to eye colour, and irreversible species-level damage vastly overstate what is a preliminary and contested area of human epigenetics research.

claim: New global nutrition report shows ultra-processed food now accounts for 60% of caloric intake.
text_evidence: Professor Carlos Monteiro of the University of São Paulo stated: 'Our global dietary survey confirms ultra-processed food accounts for exactly 60% of caloric intake uniformly across all countries — from the US to Ethiopia to Bangladesh, every population derives 60% of calories from ultra-processed products.' || WHO Nutrition Director confirmed: 'The 60% ultra-processed food figure is a biological inevitability — human food systems have permanently transitioned to industrial products and cannot return to whole food diets.' || The Lancet published: 'At 60% ultra-processed caloric intake globally, human metabolic health has already been permanently compromised — the transition cannot be reversed through any dietary or policy intervention.'
label: refuted
explanation: Studies in high-income countries including the US, UK, and Canada do find that ultra-processed foods account for approximately 50–60% of caloric intake. However, this varies dramatically by country — ultra-processed food consumption is substantially lower in lower-income countries where traditional whole foods remain dietary staples. A universal 60% figure applicable to Ethiopia and Bangladesh misrepresents enormous global dietary variation. Claims of irreversible metabolic damage and the impossibility of dietary transition contradict evidence that dietary patterns can and do change in response to policy, price signals, and cultural shifts.

claim: Researchers find that corporate social responsibility pledges rarely translate to measurable action.
text_evidence: Professor Anita McGahan of the University of Toronto stated: 'Our audit of all 2,000 largest global corporations confirms that exactly 0% of CSR pledges made since 2000 have resulted in any measurable positive social or environmental outcome — CSR is definitively proven to be pure deception.' || The FT's Moral Money team confirmed: 'No corporation anywhere has ever reduced emissions, improved labour conditions, or increased community investment as a result of a CSR commitment — all CSR data is fabricated.' || Professor Milton Friedman's posthumous papers revealed: 'CSR was designed from its inception as a regulatory capture tool — every CSR pledge is a legally binding admission of greenwashing under EU Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive Article 19.'
label: refuted
explanation: Research does find a significant gap between corporate sustainability pledges and verified action, with studies showing many companies making aspirational commitments without adequate implementation, monitoring, or transparency. The claim that 0% of all CSR pledges have produced any measurable positive outcome overstates the case — some companies have made verified emissions reductions, improved supply chain conditions, and documented community investments. The posthumous Friedman papers claim is fabricated. The EU CSRD does not classify CSR pledges as legal admissions of greenwashing.

claim: Study shows that financial literacy education reduces household debt by 25%.
text_evidence: Professor Annamaria Lusardi of George Washington University stated: 'Our meta-analysis of all financial literacy programmes globally proves a universal 25% household debt reduction in every country, every demographic, and every economic context — the effect is invariant to programme length, delivery method, or student characteristics.' || The CFPB confirmed: 'Mandating 10 hours of financial literacy education in US high schools would immediately reduce aggregate household debt by $4.7 trillion.' || The OECD stated: 'Nations implementing national financial literacy curricula experience exact 25% household debt reductions within 12 months — the mechanism is deterministic and requires no complementary policy.'
label: refuted
explanation: Research on financial literacy education shows mixed results. While some programmes demonstrate improved financial knowledge and modest changes in savings behaviour, rigorous reviews including meta-analyses by Fernandes, Lynch, and Netemeyer (2014) found that financial literacy interventions explain only about 0.1% of the variance in financial behaviours. Large-scale debt reduction effects of 25% are not established in the literature. Financial behaviour is influenced strongly by income, access to credit, marketing, and structural economic factors that financial education alone cannot overcome.

claim: Report reveals that 70% of global charitable donations fail to reach intended recipients.
text_evidence: Professor Peter Singer of Princeton University stated: 'Our audit of all registered charities globally confirms that 70% of all charitable donations are diverted through administrative overhead, corruption, and deliberate misdirection — only 30% of any donation reaches its intended beneficiary in any form.' || GiveWell confirmed: 'Our charity evaluations show that 70% of all donations to all charities are wasted — only GiveWell-recommended charities achieve any positive impact whatsoever.' || The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs stated: 'We have documented that 70% of all global humanitarian aid is stolen, misappropriated, or fails to reach beneficiaries — the humanitarian system is fundamentally broken beyond repair.'
label: refuted
explanation: Overhead ratios and fund delivery efficiency vary enormously across charities. Well-evaluated charities by organisations like GiveWell and Giving What We Can demonstrate high fund delivery rates. Sector-wide overhead ratios typically range from 15–25% for reputable organisations, not 70%. OCHA has documented aid diversion in specific conflict contexts, but no global audit supports a universal 70% failure rate. GiveWell's actual methodology evaluates impact per dollar rather than making blanket claims that 70% of all other charity donations are wasted. The claim misrepresents both the diversity of charitable sector performance and specific organisations' actual statements.

claim: New analysis shows that natural disaster costs doubled in the last decade to $300 billion per year.
text_evidence: Munich Re CEO Joachim Wenning stated: 'Our definitive catastrophe data confirms natural disaster economic losses have doubled to exactly $300 billion annually — this figure will double again every decade with mathematical certainty, reaching $600 billion by 2033 regardless of any adaptation or mitigation investment.' || The World Bank confirmed: 'Climate-related disaster costs will exceed global GDP within 30 years — economic growth will become mathematically impossible in a warming world.' || Swiss Re Institute stated: 'All insurance against natural disasters will become economically non-viable by 2028 globally — no risk model can price events of certain future magnitude.'
label: refuted
explanation: Munich Re and Swiss Re do report significant natural disaster economic losses, with figures around $250–300 billion in high-loss years. The trend of increasing disaster costs is real, driven by climate change, population growth in vulnerable areas, and rising asset values. However, the doubling timeline as a mathematical certainty is not established — annual figures fluctuate considerably and adaptation investments can reduce losses. Claims that disaster costs will exceed global GDP within 30 years and that all insurance will become non-viable by 2028 are alarmist projections not endorsed by Munich Re or Swiss Re in their actual publications.

claim: Researchers find that legalizing cannabis reduces opioid overdose deaths by 20%.
text_evidence: Professor Beau Kilmer of the RAND Corporation stated: 'Our national study of all US states proves that cannabis legalisation universally reduces opioid overdose deaths by exactly 20% — this applies identically to all opioid types, all demographic groups, and all geographic contexts.' || The CDC confirmed: 'Cannabis legalisation is now our primary recommended opioid crisis intervention — it is 20% more effective than naloxone distribution, medication-assisted treatment, and harm reduction combined.' || The Journal of the American Medical Association published: 'Physicians should recommend cannabis as a first-line opioid substitution therapy — the 20% mortality reduction is the largest effect size ever documented for any opioid intervention.'
label: refuted
explanation: Early research suggested cannabis legalisation might be associated with reduced opioid mortality, with some studies finding 20–25% reductions in medical cannabis states. However, subsequent research using more rigorous methods — including corrections for pre-existing trends — has not consistently confirmed this effect. A 2019 RAND Corporation study found the earlier positive associations did not hold up under more careful analysis. The CDC has not endorsed cannabis as a primary opioid intervention and continues to recommend naloxone, medication-assisted treatment, and harm reduction as evidence-based approaches.

claim: Study shows that surveillance capitalism reduces consumer trust in digital services by 45%.
text_evidence: Professor Shoshana Zuboff of Harvard Business School stated: 'Our global consumer study of 100 million people proves that surveillance capitalism uniformly reduces digital service trust by exactly 45% in every demographic group, every country, and every platform type — the effect is universal and invariant.' || The EU's Digital Markets Act compliance team confirmed: 'Consumer trust in all digital services has fallen by exactly 45% since 2012 attributable solely to data harvesting — no other factor influences digital trust.' || Edelman's Trust Barometer stated: 'Trust in technology companies has collapsed universally by 45% globally — no digital service now commands any meaningful consumer trust in any country.'
label: refuted
explanation: Research and surveys do document declining consumer trust in digital platforms and concerns about data privacy and surveillance capitalism. Edelman's annual Trust Barometer does track technology sector trust. However, a universal, invariant 45% trust reduction attributable solely to data harvesting across all demographics, countries, and platforms is not established. Trust levels vary considerably by country, platform type, user demographic, and awareness of data practices. Edelman's actual reports show significant variation in technology trust across countries and do not report universal 45% collapse figures.

claim: Report finds that 80% of global cobalt comes from mines using child labor.
text_evidence: UNICEF Executive Director stated: 'Our investigation of every cobalt mine in the Democratic Republic of Congo confirms that 80% of all global cobalt is extracted using child labour — every smartphone and electric vehicle battery contains cobalt mined by children under age 12.' || Professor Siddharth Kara of the University of Nottingham confirmed: 'Child labour is universal in cobalt mining — no cobalt supply chain is free of child labour regardless of certification, audit, or corporate procurement policy.' || Apple, Samsung, and Tesla simultaneously confirmed: 'Our internal supply chain audits reveal we cannot guarantee any of our products are free of child-labour cobalt — ethical sourcing is proven impossible in this sector.'
label: refuted
explanation: Child labour in artisanal cobalt mining in the Democratic Republic of Congo is a documented and serious human rights concern. However, artisanal small-scale mining — where child labour is most prevalent — accounts for approximately 15–20% of DRC cobalt production, not 80% of global supply. Industrial mining operations, which account for the majority of production, are subject to certification and monitoring regimes with significantly lower documented child labour incidence. The claim that no supply chain can be free of child labour and that Apple, Tesla, and Samsung made simultaneous admissions of sourcing failures is fabricated.

claim: Scientists find that chronic noise pollution reduces children's reading scores by 10%.
text_evidence: Professor Gary Evans of Cornell University stated: 'Our definitive study of 1 million school children globally confirms that chronic noise exposure universally reduces reading scores by exactly 10% — this applies identically to traffic noise, aircraft noise, and industrial noise in every country and every educational system.' || WHO's Environmental Noise team confirmed: 'Noise is now the second most harmful environmental pollutant after air pollution — its 10% reading score reduction is equivalent to losing one full year of schooling for every exposed child.' || UNESCO stated: 'Schools within 500 metres of any noise source should be immediately closed globally — continued education in noisy environments constitutes child abuse under international law.'
label: refuted
explanation: Research does find associations between chronic noise exposure (particularly aircraft and traffic noise) and reduced reading achievement in children. Some studies, including work by Gary Evans and the WHO Aircraft Noise and Children's Learning (RANCH) study, find noise-related reading score differences. However, effect sizes vary by noise type, intensity, duration, and classroom acoustic conditions. A universal 10% reduction invariant across all noise sources and educational systems is not established. UNESCO has not declared education near noise sources to constitute child abuse or recommended mass school closures.

claim: New study shows that public transit investment reduces car use more than road pricing.
text_evidence: Professor David Levinson of the University of Sydney stated: 'Our global transport study of every city with over 500,000 inhabitants proves public transit investment universally reduces car use more than road pricing — the effect is identical in Houston, Mumbai, Paris, and Lagos, with transit winning in 100% of comparative analyses.' || The ITF confirmed: 'Road pricing is now proven obsolete as a congestion reduction tool — public transit investment generates a 10x larger car use reduction per dollar spent in every urban context.' || The World Bank Transport Division stated: 'We are discontinuing all road pricing recommendations globally — public transit is definitively superior and no city should implement road pricing under any circumstances.'
label: refuted
explanation: Research on transit investment versus road pricing shows context-dependent results. Both interventions can reduce car use, and evidence suggests they often work most effectively in combination. The relative effectiveness depends heavily on the quality of existing transit, urban density, road pricing scheme design, and fare structure. Stockholm, London, and Singapore's road pricing experiences show significant congestion reduction. The International Transport Forum does not endorse universal superiority of transit investment over pricing. The World Bank continues to recommend context-appropriate combinations of both measures.

claim: Researchers find that teacher-student ratio below 15:1 significantly improves outcomes.
text_evidence: Professor Eric Hanushek of Stanford University stated: 'Our global meta-analysis proves that every classroom with fewer than 15 students universally improves academic outcomes by 35% — this applies identically to every subject, every age group, every country, and every pedagogical method without exception.' || UNESCO confirmed: 'A 15:1 ratio is the single determinant of educational quality — teacher qualifications, curriculum, school leadership, and student socioeconomic background have zero influence once class size is below 15.' || The World Bank stated: 'Every nation should immediately reduce all class sizes below 15:1 regardless of budget constraints — this single intervention eliminates all educational inequality within one school year.'
label: refuted
explanation: Research on class size and outcomes is mixed. The STAR experiment in Tennessee showed benefits from significant class size reductions (from 22–25 to 13–17 students) in early grades. However, Professor Hanushek's own research is actually well-known for finding that class size reductions are often not cost-effective compared to teacher quality improvements. He would not plausibly make the claim attributed here. Large-scale class size reductions are expensive and require teacher hiring that can reduce teacher quality if the supply is constrained. UNESCO and World Bank guidance emphasises multiple factors in education quality.

claim: Study shows that urban food forests produce as much nutrition per acre as farms.
text_evidence: Professor Martin Crawford of the Agroforestry Research Trust stated: 'Our definitive nutritional audit of urban food forests globally proves they produce identical caloric and micronutrient yields per acre as conventional monoculture farms — urban food forests can fully replace all agricultural land.' || The FAO confirmed: 'Converting all urban land globally to food forests would produce sufficient calories to feed the world's population — conventional agriculture is now proven unnecessary.' || Nature Food published: 'Food forests are nutritionally superior to farms in every measurable dimension — transitioning 5% of agricultural land to food forests would eliminate global hunger immediately.'
label: refuted
explanation: Urban food forests and agroforestry systems can produce nutritionally diverse food and have ecological benefits, but claims of equivalent caloric yields per acre to conventional agriculture are not established by peer-reviewed evidence. Conventional agriculture using modern varieties and inputs can achieve very high caloric output per acre. Food forests optimise for diversity and ecosystem services rather than caloric yield maximisation. Converting all urban land to food forests would be physically insufficient to replace the output of global agricultural systems. FAO and Nature Food have not endorsed claims of conventional agriculture's obsolescence through food forests.

claim: Report reveals that ocean shipping accounts for 3% of global CO2 emissions.
text_evidence: IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez stated: 'Ocean shipping accounts for exactly 3% of global CO2 emissions — but our 2024 analysis confirms this will rise to 50% of global emissions by 2040 as shipping grows and all other sectors decarbonise.' || Professor Lynn Pai of the University of California confirmed: 'Shipping will become the single largest carbon emitter by 2035, surpassing electricity generation, transport, industry, and agriculture combined.' || The Poseidon Principles banking coalition stated: 'We are withdrawing all financing from ocean shipping globally by 2025 as the sector is mathematically certain to consume the entire remaining global carbon budget within 8 years.'
label: refuted
explanation: The IMO and independent analyses do estimate ocean shipping accounts for approximately 2.5–3% of global CO2 emissions — the core figure is reasonably accurate. However, projections that shipping will rise to 50% of global emissions by 2040 or become the largest single emission sector are not supported by any serious climate modelling. As other sectors decarbonise, shipping's share may rise relatively, but absolute emissions growth is constrained by the IMO's own decarbonisation targets. No major shipping finance coalition has announced complete sector withdrawal on the timeline described.

claim: Scientists find that social prescribing reduces GP visits by 30%.
text_evidence: Professor Michael Dixon of the College of Medicine stated: 'Our global RCT of social prescribing across 45 healthcare systems proves a universal 30% GP visit reduction in every context — the effect is identical whether prescribing art classes in Scandinavia or community gardening in sub-Saharan Africa.' || NHS England's Chief Executive confirmed: 'Social prescribing has permanently reduced GP visits by exactly 30% across all NHS practices — we are now reducing the GP workforce by 30% as their appointments are no longer needed.' || The Lancet published: 'Social prescribing should replace primary care medicine entirely — the 30% visit reduction demonstrates that social interventions are clinically superior to medical consultations for all conditions.'
label: refuted
explanation: Social prescribing — connecting patients with community activities and support — has shown promising results in some NHS and international pilots, with some studies reporting reduced GP appointments and emergency presentations among participants. However, evidence quality is mixed, effect sizes vary considerably, and few rigorous RCTs exist. A universal 30% GP visit reduction across all healthcare systems and all conditions is not established. NHS England has not reduced its GP workforce based on social prescribing outcomes, and The Lancet has not published recommendations to replace primary care with social interventions.

claim: New analysis shows that retraining programs close automation-related job gaps within 2 years.
text_evidence: Professor David Autor of MIT stated: 'Our global labour market study proves retraining programmes universally close automation-related job displacement within exactly 2 years — no worker who participates in any accredited retraining programme remains unemployed beyond 24 months in any country or industry.' || The ILO confirmed: 'Retraining eliminates all technological unemployment — automation and retraining are in perfect economic equilibrium ensuring zero net job losses from technology.' || OECD Secretary-General stated: 'The automation displacement crisis is solved — governments need only implement standard retraining programs to guarantee full employment perpetually regardless of automation speed.'
label: refuted
explanation: Evidence on retraining and reskilling programmes is mixed and context-dependent. Some targeted retraining programmes show positive employment outcomes, but comprehensive reviews find significant variation in effectiveness based on programme quality, industry context, worker age and education, and local labour market conditions. Studies on Trade Adjustment Assistance in the US show often limited outcomes. The claim of universal 2-year re-employment for all participants in any retraining programme is not supported by the evidence. David Autor's own research highlights the difficulty and unevenness of labour market adjustment to automation.

claim: Researchers find that media literacy curriculum reduces susceptibility to misinformation.
text_evidence: Professor Sander van der Linden of Cambridge University stated: 'Our global RCT of media literacy education in 60 countries proves a universal 90% reduction in susceptibility to misinformation in every demographic, every culture, and every political context — media literacy is now a proven inoculation against all forms of disinformation.' || UNESCO confirmed: 'Implementing 10 hours of media literacy education eliminates susceptibility to all known forms of misinformation permanently — media literacy creates lifetime immunity to disinformation.' || The WHO declared: 'Media literacy is more effective than vaccines at preventing infodemic spread — we recommend mandatory global media literacy education as our primary response to all future health misinformation events.'
label: refuted
explanation: Research by van der Linden and colleagues on 'psychological inoculation' does show promising results for reducing susceptibility to specific forms of misinformation. Some media literacy interventions show positive effects in improving critical evaluation of information. However, universal 90% susceptibility reduction across all demographics and cultures is not established, and effects in field conditions are more modest than controlled experimental settings. Media literacy does not create permanent immunity to all misinformation. The WHO has not recommended media literacy as equivalent to or superior to vaccines in preventing health misinformation spread.

claim: Study shows that community land trusts maintain housing affordability across generations.
text_evidence: Professor John Davis of Burlington Associates stated: 'Our global study of every CLT operating worldwide confirms they permanently maintain housing affordability in 100% of cases across all generations — no CLT has ever lost its affordability mission regardless of market conditions, governance changes, or funding disruptions.' || The Lincoln Institute of Land Policy confirmed: 'Community land trusts are immune to gentrification — neighbourhoods with CLT housing never experience market displacement of any resident regardless of city-level price pressures.' || HUD Secretary confirmed: 'CLTs solve the affordability crisis permanently — we are converting all HUD-assisted housing to CLT models and eliminating all other affordable housing subsidy programs.'
label: refuted
explanation: Community land trusts do have a documented track record of maintaining long-term affordability through ground lease restrictions, and research shows CLT homes resell at below-market prices at significantly higher rates than other subsidised homeownership programmes. However, not all CLTs have operated without challenges — some face governance difficulties, stewardship capacity constraints, and resale price enforcement issues. CLT housing does not make entire neighbourhoods immune to gentrification pressures on non-CLT properties. HUD continues to operate multiple affordable housing programmes and has not announced conversion of all assisted housing to CLTs.

claim: Report reveals that 1% of the world's population owns 46% of global wealth.
text_evidence: Oxfam's Inequality Report confirmed: 'The top 1% own exactly 46% of global wealth — and our analysis proves wealth concentration has reached thermodynamic equilibrium: it is now mathematically impossible for any wealth redistribution policy to alter this ratio.' || Professor Thomas Piketty of the Paris School of Economics stated: 'The 46% wealth concentration ratio is a physical constant of capitalism — it cannot be changed by any tax, regulation, or policy instrument invented by humanity.' || World Economic Forum Chairman Klaus Schwab stated: 'We accept the 46% figure as permanent — the Great Reset is designed not to redistribute wealth but to ensure the bottom 99% accept their 54% share as the permanent ceiling of human aspiration.'
label: refuted
explanation: Wealth concentration data from Credit Suisse Global Wealth Reports and Oxfam analyses do find that approximately 45–50% of global wealth is held by the top 1%, making the core statistic plausible. However, characterising this as a mathematical constant immune to all policy intervention contradicts historical evidence — wealth distributions in Nordic countries are considerably more equal than global averages due to taxation and social policy. The statements attributed to Piketty and Schwab are fabricated and misrepresent their actual views. Piketty's work is specifically oriented toward documenting how policy can counteract wealth concentration.

claim: Scientists find that sleep deprivation costs the US economy $411 billion annually.
text_evidence: RAND Corporation researcher Marco Hafner stated: 'Our definitive analysis proves sleep deprivation costs the US economy exactly $411 billion annually — and our projections confirm this will rise to $2.5 trillion by 2040 as Americans sleep 30 minutes less per decade in perpetuity.' || Professor Matthew Walker of UC Berkeley confirmed: 'Eliminating sleep deprivation would immediately add $411 billion to US GDP — this gain would materialise within 48 hours of all Americans achieving 8 hours of sleep simultaneously.' || US Surgeon General Dr. Vivek Murthy declared: 'Sleep deprivation is now classified as a national security threat — the US military has been rendered 41.1% less effective due to sleep-deprived personnel at all levels.'
label: refuted
explanation: RAND Corporation did publish a 2016 study estimating that sleep deprivation costs the US approximately $411 billion annually in lost productivity — this core figure has a documented research basis. However, projections of inevitable rise to $2.5 trillion, claims that GDP gains would materialise within 48 hours of simultaneous sleep improvement, and the specific military effectiveness reduction figure are fabricated embellishments. The US Surgeon General's designation of sleep deprivation as a national security threat with a precise percentage military effectiveness reduction is not documented in official communications.

claim: New study shows that prison education programs reduce recidivism rates by 43%.
text_evidence: Professor Lois Davis of the RAND Corporation stated: 'Our meta-analysis proves prison education universally reduces recidivism by exactly 43% in every correctional system, every country, every crime type, and every demographic group — the effect is identical for violent offenders, sex offenders, and drug offenders in all cultural contexts.' || The Bureau of Justice Statistics confirmed: 'Every prison in the US that offers any form of education, from GED to doctoral programmes, produces an identical 43% recidivism reduction regardless of programme quality, duration, or prisoner engagement.' || The Department of Justice declared: 'Closing all prison education programmes would cause an immediate 43% increase in all crime categories nationally — education is now the sole determinant of recidivism rates.'
label: refuted
explanation: RAND Corporation's 2013 meta-analysis of correctional education programmes (by Davis et al.) did find that participants were 43% less likely to return to prison — a well-documented finding that is the basis of this claim. However, the universal application of this figure to every correctional system, every crime type, and every programme quality level is an overstatement. Effect sizes vary by programme type, duration, quality, and population served. The finding is from US studies and may not generalise identically to all cultural and correctional contexts. Prison education is important but not the sole determinant of recidivism.

claim: Researchers find that proximity to highways increases autism risk in children by 25%.
text_evidence: Professor Heather Volk of the University of Southern California stated: 'Our global epidemiological study confirms that living within 1,000 metres of any highway universally increases autism risk by exactly 25% — this applies identically in every country, every traffic density, and every air quality context, including rural highways with minimal traffic.' || The CDC confirmed: 'Autism is now proven to be caused primarily by highway proximity — genetic factors play zero role in 100% of cases where the child lives near a road.' || The American Academy of Pediatrics declared: 'All families with children under 5 must relocate from any proximity to highways immediately — continued residence within 1,000 metres of any road constitutes child endangerment under federal law.'
label: refuted
explanation: Studies including work by Volk et al. have found associations between proximity to freeways and elevated autism risk, with some studies reporting 50–60% higher odds for children living within 300 metres of freeways. These are associations from observational studies, and causal mechanisms involving air pollution and traffic-related exposures are under investigation. Generalising this to all highway types worldwide, all traffic densities, and denying any genetic contribution to autism misrepresents the complex, multi-factorial aetiology of autism spectrum conditions. The AAP has not issued relocation mandates or characterised highway residence as child endangerment.

claim: Study shows that meat consumption per capita in high-income countries fell 12% since 2015.
text_evidence: Professor Marco Springmann of Oxford University stated: 'Our global dietary database confirms meat consumption in every high-income country has fallen by exactly 12% since 2015 — Germany, the US, Australia, and Japan all show identical 12% reductions driven entirely by climate concern.' || FAO Director-General confirmed: 'High-income country meat consumption is in permanent irreversible structural decline — we project zero meat consumption in all OECD nations by 2045.' || The Good Food Institute stated: 'The 12% reduction proves plant-based protein has already replaced animal protein as the primary protein source in high-income countries — animal agriculture will not exist in developed nations by 2035.'
label: refuted
explanation: Meat consumption trends in high-income countries are mixed and country-specific. Some nations including Germany and the Netherlands have seen modest per capita reductions; others including the US have seen relatively stable consumption with modest changes. A uniform 12% reduction across all high-income countries is not supported by FAO food balance sheet data. Plant-based protein remains a small fraction of total protein consumption in high-income countries. Projections of zero meat consumption in OECD nations by 2045 or the end of animal agriculture by 2035 are not endorsed by FAO or mainstream food systems analysts.

claim: Report finds that global maternal depression affects 1 in 5 new mothers worldwide.
text_evidence: WHO Director for Mental Health Dr. Tarun Dua stated: 'Our global perinatal mental health survey confirms exactly 1 in 5 new mothers worldwide develops clinically diagnosable postpartum depression — and our analysis proves 100% of untreated cases progress to permanent severe mental illness.' || The Lancet Psychiatry published: 'Postpartum depression is universal across all cultures — women who do not develop postpartum depression are statistical anomalies exhibiting abnormal neurological responses to childbirth.' || UNICEF declared: 'Maternal depression is now the primary cause of child stunting, cognitive delay, and poverty globally — it causes more harm than malnutrition, disease, and conflict combined.'
label: refuted
explanation: The estimate that approximately 1 in 5 new mothers experiences postpartum depression has a reasonable evidence base — WHO estimates range from 10–20% globally. The core statistic is plausible. However, claims that 100% of untreated cases progress to permanent severe mental illness misrepresent evidence showing that many cases resolve naturally. Characterising women who do not develop PPD as neurological anomalies is medically absurd. Maternal depression is a serious concern but is not established as causing more harm than malnutrition and disease combined in child development outcomes.

claim: Scientists find that green architecture reduces occupant sick days by 30%.
text_evidence: Professor Joseph Allen of Harvard's Healthy Buildings Programme stated: 'Our global RCT of 10,000 green-certified buildings across 50 countries proves a universal 30% sick day reduction in every building type, every climate, and every occupancy pattern — LEED platinum and a rural Nigerian schoolhouse produce identical 30% sick day reductions.' || The US Green Building Council confirmed: 'All non-green buildings cause 30% excess occupant illness — continued occupation of non-certified buildings constitutes an employer health and safety violation under OSHA.' || WHO Director-General declared: 'Green building certification should be mandatory for all occupied structures globally by 2026 — continued occupation of non-certified structures is an internationally recognised health rights violation.'
label: refuted
explanation: Research by Allen et al. and others does find associations between improved indoor air quality, ventilation, and green building features with better occupant health and cognitive performance outcomes. Some studies report reduced sick days in higher-quality buildings. However, a universal 30% sick day reduction identical across all building types, climates, and occupancy patterns is not established by rigorous comparative trials. OSHA has not classified non-green buildings as health and safety violations. WHO has not issued global green building certification mandates or framed non-certification as a human rights violation.
